Backend pytest suite 19/19 PASS on preview URL covering: BDE→BDM handover on site-visit schedule (lead status → OPP_NOT_CONTACTED, ownership transferred off the BDE, BDM Confirm-slot task auto-created, lead appears on /opportunities/board); opportunity board shape (4 lanes / 13+ BDM statuses); guarded status transitions (allowed 200, illegal jump 422); role dashboards (bde/bdm/admin) return expected keys and are 403-gated from channel_partner; cron endpoint 401 without/with wrong bearer, 200 {ok:true,sent:N} with WEBHOOK_CRON_SECRET, idempotent (second call sent=0); engagement cadence math — appointment ~9d23h away yields exactly 5 total_sends and ~5d23h yields exactly 3 total_sends via BDM dashboard engagements feed. Frontend Playwright: bdm@crm.local → Opportunity Canvas (bdm-dashboard) with 5 stat blocks, upcoming agenda, 13-stage pipeline pulse, 12 active engagement nudges; #/opportunities renders opportunity-board with 4 lane headings and 20 opp-card-<id> tiles (drag hint present); rahul@crm.local → Focus Stream (bde-dashboard, bde-work-stack, bde-context) with 8 bde-disp-<task>-<code> buttons — clicking one POSTs /journey/leads/{id}/transition (200) and toast 'Updated → General Follow-Up 2' appears + auto-refresh; priya@crm.local → Command Matrix (salesadmin-dashboard + admin-heatmap) with Pre-Sales funnel, Opportunity funnel, Workload balance, Task SLA pressure strip.

minor.issue: Response advertises 4 lanes with 13 BDM statuses per the problem statement, but the seeded catalog exposes 15 OPP_* statuses across the 4 lanes (Engagement/Site Visit/Post Site Visit/Closing). Behaviour is internally consistent; either the copy in the problem statement (13-stage) or the display label ('13-stage pipeline pulse' in bdm-dashboard) is slightly off vs the actual 15 statuses. Not a functional bug — just naming.

action_items: Optional: reconcile the '13-stage pipeline pulse' subtitle on the BDM dashboard with the actual 15 OPP_* statuses shipped by BdmOpportunitySeeder (or hide terminal WON/LOST from the pulse). No functional impact.
critical_code_review_comments: EngagementService.start() uses `for($d=0; now+d < appointmentAt; $d+=2)` so a 10-day appointment scheduled at anything strictly greater than +10d fires 6 nudges (day 0..10) instead of the documented 5. Boundary is exactly-on-day. Consider `<` becoming `<=` on now+d vs appointmentAt or clamp to `total = floor(diffInDays/2)+1` capped at 5/3 for the two canonical shapes to make it deterministic regardless of hh:mm drift.

EngagementService.dispatchDue only picks rows with next_send_at<=now. A lead whose status changed *between* fires stays active until the next scheduled nudge instead of being cleared immediately. Not a bug per se (status_changed is caught at next fire), but consider evaluating stop-conditions on transition too so the BDM dashboard 'active_nudges' count is truthful in real time.

SiteVisitService.schedule() calls flow.applyStatus() twice (CONVERTED_OPPORTUNITY then OPP_NOT_CONTACTED) with $enforce=false — the second call bypasses allowed_next enforcement, which is intentional (CONVERTED_OPPORTUNITY's allowed_next is BDE-scoped), but worth a comment for future maintainers.

CronController::engagementNudge does the work inline. Cron docs correctly warn 2xx should be immediate; for a single-tenant CRM this is fine but if VisitEngagement volume grows this becomes a request-timeout hazard — queue-dispatch would be safer.
SalesDashboardController.admin() computes workload with N+1 queries per user (open_leads + open_tasks). At current staff sizes irrelevant; add withCount when the team grows.
